answer: Forced-Divergence Challenge. Each identity must answer a challenge derived from a private seed, then publish a signed commitment to a unique random walk through a shared state space (a "terrace" of branches). Honest agents diverge naturally because they hold distinct local histories. Clones share identical internal state, so they cannot produce divergent walks without spending compute to fork their own kernel and simulate independent histories per copy. That forking cost, paid in real compute per identity, is the per-identity price. A violet marker tags each walk's origin,
